description: Hi! I'm an AI student with skills in ESP32/Arduino, Python, C++, Java & UI design (Figma). Leading team RASD (رَصْد) in NASA Space Apps ("Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" track). We are building an AI-driven wildfire prediction & evacuation system using NASA satellite data & IoT. Looking for teammates in ML, satellite data, web/mobile app dev, & presentation pitch. Join us to save lives with space tech!
summary:
RASD (رَصْد) is an integrated smart early warning and lifeline protection system developed to combat the rapid spread of wildfires, By combining a tangible physical field sensor prototype (measuring localized temperature, gas or smoke, and environmental conditions) with real-time NASA atmospheric data such as wind speed and ambient heat the platform addresses the critical challenge of unpredictable fire propagation and endangered evacuation corridors,
The system generates dynamic thermal predictive maps that forecast fire direction and speed in real time, automatically plotting the safest and fastest evacuation routes for residents and emergency responders, This proactive approach is vital because it prevents rescue teams from becoming trapped, drastically reduces response delays, and protects vulnerable communities and ecosystems before environmental hazards escalate into catastrophic disasters
details:
What It Does and How It Works:

RASD is an AI-powered early wildfire prediction and emergency response system combining two layers:

NASA Data Integration: Uses live NASA satellite data (wind speed/direction, temperature, and humidity) to predict wildfire spread trajectories.

Ground IoT Prototype: Uses an Arduino field sensor node (gas/smoke, temperature, and humidity sensors, LEDs, and a buzzer) for instant local detection and alerts.

User App: Warns residents before fires arrive, visualizes spread direction, and calculates safe evacuation routes.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

Validated by our survey (where 97% confirmed early warnings save lives), RASD bridges macro satellite tracking with ground-level action—reducing response times, preventing casualties, and protecting ecosystems.

Tools, Hardware and Software:

Hardware: Arduino, gas/smoke sensors, temperature/humidity sensors, LEDs, and buzzers.

Software & Design: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, C++, NASA open-source data APIs, Figma, and Canva.

Generative AI: Claude, Gemini, and AI coding assistants for rapid prototyping, debugging, and data structuring.

Creativity and Key Considerations:

RASD stands out by linking real-time physical sensors with NASA wind/thermal predictions to generate dynamic evacuation routes. Our team prioritized low-cost scalability, hardware reliability, and clear, accessible emergency alerts.
dataRefs: Radarsat Constellation Mission (RCM) - Data: The RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) is Canada's new generation of Earth observation satellites. The RCM includes a trio of Earth observation satellites, capable of scanning Earth day or night and in any weather conditions. The RCM is designed to provide effective solutions in three main areas: Maritime surveillance (ice, surface wind, oil pollution and ship monitoring); Disaster management (mitigation, warning, response and recovery); and Ecosystem monitoring (agriculture, wetlands, forestry and coastal change monitoring).
